finding: There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so this is a first build, not a check. HELD: the luxury class has no stated labor time and only one parts page; the economy class has no manufacturer-stated time printed with a unit, so its high end is null; and only two independent estimates for the gasket job itself were found (the third benchmark is for a different job). Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks), each for one manifold or one side: midsize 2019 Dodge Durango 5.7L about $376-$601 (2.9-3.5 hr); truck 2019 Ram 1500 5.7L about $184-$584 (1.3-3.4 hr); economy 2012 Honda Civic 1.8L about $127 at the low end only (1.0 hr), high end not built; luxury not built. Against the benchmarks: RepairPal's national $417-$596 overlaps the top of both built ranges, and YourMechanic's 2016 Durango 5.7L figures ($414 mobile, $483-$634 at a shop) sit close to our Durango $376-$601. The gasket itself is cheap everywhere ($7-$41 here, $41-$45 at RepairPal); almost all of the price is labor. How solid the labor times are: the midsize and truck figures are FCA warranty times for the example vehicles, printed in hours, but they are for replacing the manifold with a kit, not for refitting the old manifold with a new gasket. The manifold comes off and goes back on in both jobs, so the time carries over, but the kit also includes a tie bar and heat shield, and a reviewer may prefer to treat these as cross-checks. The truck range is wide because the same engine takes 1.3-1.6 hours in the older Ram 1500 Classic body and 3.1-3.4 hours in the new body. The economy low end is a signed general statement ('might take an hour' for an easy front-mount four-cylinder), not a book time; two GM bulletins for four-cylinder engines print 0.9 and 1.2 with no unit and are kept as cross-checks only. Warranty times are the low end of what a shop bills, and none of these figures includes freeing rusted or broken studs, which is the usual reason this job runs over.
held_reason: Luxury: no stated labor time and one parts source. Economy: high end of hours is null (no manufacturer time printed with a unit for any four-cylinder car; the low end is a general signed statement). Midsize and truck hours are manufacturer times for replacing the manifold with a kit, used for the gasket job because the removal and refitting are the same; confirm that reading before publishing. Only two independent benchmarks for the gasket job itself.
extras: A quote often adds diagnosis of the exhaust leak, shop supplies and sales tax. Broken or seized studs and bolts are common on this job and are charged as extra labor, sometimes by the hour, with new studs, bolts or nuts. A cracked or warped manifold means a new manifold or machining the old one. Heat shields, the gasket where the manifold meets the exhaust pipe or catalytic converter, and oxygen sensors that will not come out cleanly can also be added. On a V6 or V8 the other side is a second job at about the same price, and four-wheel-drive trucks can carry extra labor.
